edges.description: Prlr-null mice lose dopaminergic inhibition of the pituitary.
edges.limitations: Null mice model complete receptor loss, whereas most reported patients are heterozygous, and the mice develop prolactinomas that patients do not.

edges.description: Prlr-null females are sterile from implantation failure.
edges.limitations: Complete receptor loss in mice; the human evidence is a single heterozygous carrier, and the biallelic patient had two pregnancies.

edges.description: Null mice reproduce the prolactin hypersecretion.
edges.limitations: Female null mice go on to develop lactotroph hyperplasia and large prolactinomas, which no patient has shown on MRI.

edges.description: Halved receptor dosage impairs mammary development and first lactation.
edges.limitations: The defect is age- and parity-dependent in mice, and the one heterozygous human carrier described lactated normally; agalactia in humans is reported only with biallelic loss.

nodes.description: Complete absence of lactation after delivery in a woman with biallelic PRLR loss of function.

evidence.reference_title: Variant Prolactin Receptor in Agalactia and Hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: Here we describe a 35-year-old woman who presented with idiopathic hyperprolactinemia that was associated with a complete lack of lactation after each of her two deliveries.

nodes.description: Primary infertility, reported in one sister despite normal ovulatory cycles.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant prolactin receptor and familial hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: However, the 38-year-old sister described here had infertility but normal ovulatory cycles, thereby implicating another role for prolactin and the prolactin receptor in regulating fertility.

nodes.description: Persistent elevation of serum prolactin without a pituitary lesion, macroprolactin negative. It appears after puberty and is higher in women than in men.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant prolactin receptor and familial hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: The hyperprolactinemia in this pedigree was found only in postpubertal family members, and the serum prolactin concentrations were higher in women than in men

nodes.description: Prolactin no longer activates JAK2 and STAT5 through the mutant receptor, and STAT5-dependent gene expression is lost. Co-expression of mutant and wild-type receptors also reduces signalling, consistent with haploinsufficiency or a dominant-negative effect in heterozygotes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant prolactin receptor and familial hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: Cotransfection with non-mutant His188 and mutant Arg188 PRLR constructs resulted in a reduction of CISH reporter expression, which is consistent with a loss of function and a probable dominant-negative action of the mutant prolactin receptor

nodes.description: With reduced dopaminergic inhibition and loss of direct autocrine/paracrine restraint, pituitary lactotrophs secrete excess prolactin. Patients have no pituitary lesion on MRI, unlike Prlr-null mice, which develop lactotroph hyperplasia and prolactinomas.

nodes.description: Prolactin normally acts on PRLR in hypothalamic tuberoinfundibular dopamine neurons to increase dopamine release onto lactotrophs. Without receptor signalling, dopamine tone on the pituitary falls.

evidence.reference_title: Lack of prolactin receptor signaling in mice results in lactotroph proliferation and prolactinomas by dopamine-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: Pharmacologic studies in Prlr(-/-) mice with D2R agonists and antagonists demonstrated a significant loss of endogenous dopamine tone, i.e., constitutive inhibitory signaling by the D2R, in the pituitary.

evidence.reference_title: Elevated Prolactin during Pregnancy Drives a Phenotypic Switch in Mouse Hypothalamic Dopaminergic Neurons.
evidence.snippet: These neurons normally release dopamine to inhibit prolactin secretion and are activated by prolactin in a short-loop feedback manner.

nodes.description: Mammary epithelium cannot respond to prolactin, so lactation fails despite high prolactin. In humans this is reported with biallelic loss; a heterozygous His188Arg carrier lactated after each of four pregnancies. Heterozygous Prlr-knockout mice show a dosage effect, failing to lactate after a first pregnancy but not after later ones.

evidence.reference_title: Null mutation of the prolactin receptor gene produces multiple reproductive defects in the mouse.
evidence.snippet: Heterozygous females showed almost complete failure of lactation attributable to greatly reduced mammary gland development after their first, but not subsequent, pregnancies.

meta.association: Germline loss-of-function PRLR variants: heterozygous His188Arg in the high-affinity ligand-binding interface, and compound heterozygous Arg171Ter/Pro269Leu.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant prolactin receptor and familial hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the familial hyperprolactinemia appears to be due to a germline, loss-of-function mutation in PRLR, resulting in prolactin insensitivity.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of prolactin receptor variants with diverse effects on receptor signalling.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, an inactivating germline heterozygous PRLR variant (His188Arg) was reported in a kindred with hyperprolactinaemia, while an inactivating compound heterozygous PRLR variant (Pro269Leu/Arg171Stop) was identified in an individual with hyperprolactinaemia and agalactia.

nodes.description: Germline PRLR variants abolish prolactin-receptor signalling. His188Arg removes a histidine at the high-affinity binding site 1 interface; the mutant receptor is expressed and localised normally but does not signal.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant prolactin receptor and familial hyperprolactinemia.
evidence.snippet: This substitution disrupted the high-affinity ligand-binding interface of the prolactin receptor, resulting in a loss of downstream signaling by Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) and signal transducer and activator of transcription 5 (STAT5).

nodes.description: Heterozygous Prlr-knockout females have smaller, less branched mammary glands and fail to lactate after a first pregnancy when mated young.

evidence.reference_title: Mammary gland development in prolactin receptor knockout mice.
evidence.snippet: Histological and whole mount analysis of virgin mammary glands showed that heterozygous glands were smaller in size due to a less developed ductal structure with fewer branch points.

nodes.description: Mice lacking the prolactin receptor develop hyperprolactinemia with loss of pituitary dopamine tone, and females develop large prolactinomas.

evidence.reference_title: Lack of prolactin receptor signaling in mice results in lactotroph proliferation and prolactinomas by dopamine-dependent and -independent mechanisms.
evidence.snippet: The absence of either receptor induced hyperprolactinemia and large prolactinomas in females.

nodes.description: In rodents prolactin is luteotrophic and its receptor is required for embryonic implantation; in humans the corpus luteum is LH-dependent, and prolactin's reproductive-tract role is less defined. Loss of receptor signalling is proposed to impair fertility independently of ovulation: one heterozygous carrier was infertile with normal ovulatory cycles, and Prlr-null female mice are sterile from implantation failure. The human step is inferred, not demonstrated.

evidence.snippet: Indeed, prolactin and the prolactin receptor have been reported to have roles in the luteal phase and peri-implantation period, and abnormalities of circulating prolactin have been associated with early pregnancy loss.
